root_cause.text: The switch statement in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` did not handle masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`), causing a fallthrough to the default case that returns NULL for `rm` while `send->s_op` remains set, leading to a NULL pointer dereference in `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the two masked atomic opcodes to the same case as their non-masked counterparts, and the commit message states: "But the completion-side switch in rds_ib_send_unmap_op() only handles the non-masked opcodes, so a masked atomic completion falls through to default and returns rm == NULL while send->s_op is left set. rds_ib_send_cqe_handler() then dereferences the NULL rm via rm->m_final_op."

Author: Andy Grover <andy.grover@oracle.com>

    RDS: Perform unmapping ops in stages
    
    Previously, RDS would wait until the final send WR had completed
    and then handle cleanup. With silent ops, we do not know
    if an atomic, rdma, or data op will be last. This patch
    handles any of these cases by keeping a pointer to the last

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` with a switch on `send->s_wr.opcode` that only handles `IB_WR_SEND`, `IB_WR_RDMA_WRITE`, `IB_WR_RDMA_READ`, `IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD`, and `IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`. It does not handle `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` or `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`. Consequently, masked atomic opcodes fall into the default case, which returns NULL for `rm` without clearing `send->s_op`. The caller `rds_ib_send_cq_comp_handler()` then dereferences `rm` via `&send->s_op == &rm->m_final_op`, leading to a NULL pointer dereference. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
